selected_bottleneck: apply-persisted-change-count-integrity（应用持久化变更数量完整性）
selected_problem: Fresh canonical main required a non-empty change list and capped it at MAX_FILES=128 while staging, but apply trusted the persisted changes array after reload. A rewritten empty list could be marked APPLIED as a no-op, while a coherently expanded list could execute more than 128 workspace mutations and bypass the stage-time file-count budget.
decision_basis: CHANGES_REQUIRED and TOO_MANY_CHANGES are already explicit stage-time protocol constraints, so revalidating them at apply preserves an existing invariant rather than inventing a new budget policy.
Both defects are directly falsifiable with a durable STAGED document and can be rejected before any workspace side effect.
Hosted Developer Execution Runtime remained temporarily unavailable with HTTP 502; this cycle used DWAC_SOURCE_CONTRACT_REPLAY（DWAC 源码契约重放） and exact local focused validation.

pre_fix_reality.empty_case: EXPECTED_FAILURE: apply accepted an empty persisted changes array and reported the changeset as APPLIED.
pre_fix_reality.over_budget_case: EXPECTED_FAILURE: apply accepted 129 persisted unique writes and created all files, bypassing the stage-time MAX_FILES limit.
pre_fix_reality.impact: Durable reload could erase both the semantic non-empty requirement and the bounded side-effect count that stage had approved.

change: Apply now requires doc.changes to remain an array with at least one entry and at most MAX_FILES entries before constructing any preflight state or touching the workspace.

validation.node_check: PASS on the exact proposed core/changesets.mjs content
validation.focused_tests: 10/10 PASS, 0 skipped across apply-preimage, operation, path-set, path-canonicality, and change-count integrity
validation.pre_fix_regressions: Both empty and over-budget cases reproduced before the fix
validation.no_side_effect: PASS: rejected over-budget artifact creates neither the first nor last candidate file

truth_boundary: This preserves the stage-time change-count contract across durable reload. It does not yet revalidate persisted per-file or aggregate byte budgets and is not an authenticated artifact mechanism.
